title: Legacy Financial Ledger Modernization
business: A regional bank managing a monolithic COBOL-based ledger system that requires migration to a modern microservices architecture.
problem: The bank cannot migrate its legacy ledger due to strict regulatory requirements prohibiting the transmission of sensitive financial data to public cloud-based AI coding assistants, leading to slow manual refactoring.
solution: The bank deploys the Laguna model family within its air-gapped VPC using Poolside's self-managed inference. This allows the bank to utilize agentic workflows to analyze legacy codebases and propose modern service interfaces without data ever leaving the secure perimeter.
steps: Provision the Laguna model weights within the bank's air-gapped infrastructure.
Configure Poolside agent instructions to define the target microservice architecture standards.
Utilize the Poolside Agent CLI to execute automated refactoring tasks on isolated code modules.
Implement approval prompts within the agent workflow to ensure human oversight for all generated code changes.
Validate the refactored code against existing test suites using the controlled execution environment.
outcome: The bank achieves a secure, accelerated migration path for its legacy ledger while maintaining full compliance with data sovereignty regulations and internal security policies.
limitation: Self-managed inference requires significant internal compute resources; performance is limited by the hardware provisioned within the VPC, which must be monitored to ensure agent latency remains within acceptable thresholds for developer productivity.
